comment: Explicit record selection for the T1 item 8 characterization report
(signoff/characterization/generate.py; see README.md beside this file).
Every record the report reads is named here BY PATH and PINNED BY SHA-256.
Nothing is discovered by globbing or by filesystem modification time: a
newer record under sim/*/records/ changes nothing until this file is
edited to select it (and its pin refreshed), and a selected record whose
bytes changed is an error, not a silent re-read.
A Monte Carlo record may also pin the raw per-draw population behind its
summary (`draws_csv` + `draws_csv_sha256`, always together; a draws file
is never named without its hash pin). Naming draws opts the record into
the statistics audit (definition check `offset_mc_statistics`): every
published per-point statistic is recomputed from the pinned draws, exactly
as sim/input-offset/run_offset_mc.sh computes it, and must match to the
bench's printf %.9g serialization. A drifted draws file, an altered
summary statistic, or an incomplete/duplicated/non-finite population is
an error naming the point and field, never a silent pass.
The CMRR mismatch record pins a LIST of raw sample files instead
(`mc_samples`: one `<point>_mc_samples.txt` per grid point, each with its
sha256, plus the bench acceptance thresholds and the `av0_join` record the
bench joined Av0 from). It opts into definition check
`cmrr_mc_statistics`: counts, linear-domain Acm mean/sigma and the DR-0004
bound are recomputed offline with sim/cmrr-mismatch/mc_samples.py
point_stats and must match the summary at the bench's printf %.6g
(issue #208). It is not forced through the offset draws CSV contract.
The input-noise record pins, per grid point, its raw ngspice log and in-band
spectrum (`noise_raw`: sha256 per file, plus the documented band). It opts
into definition check `noise_raw_audit` (issue #213): the logged integrated
noise (`vni_int_vrms`, a verbatim log token) and the spectrum-derived
quantities (spot densities, flicker/thermal split, corner, cross-check) are
recomputed offline with sim/input-noise/noise_post.py -- the module the
bench runs -- and checked independently, at the bench's serialization.
Each `rows[]` entry is one claimed quantity. `class` is one of:
ratified   -- a bound ratified in spec/target-spec.md section 2 (binding);
superseded -- a ratified bound that a later decision record superseded,
kept as context exactly as the spec keeps it in-row (not
binding: it never fails the overall verdict);
measured   -- a measured but UNRATIFIED quantity ([P] or 'Measured (not
yet ratified)'): reported with its evidence, never given a
pass/fail verdict;
pending    -- a spec row with no evidence by construction (Area).
`load_condition` is structured ({cl, applicability: applies|dc_ignored,
note}); the displayed load is derived after `cl` is checked against the
ratified spec CL and the pinned source record's stated CL (README.md,
"Load (CL) validation"). `conditions` stays descriptive prose.
`bound.value` is copied VERBATIM from the ratified spec text and the
generator refuses a row whose `spec_check.text` (which must contain that
literal) is not present on the named spec/target-spec.md row. It is also
the comparison precision: see `comparison_rule` in the generated report.
`inventory_label` ties each row to its line in
signoff/evidence/testbenches.txt (the item 9 record map); the selected
record must be the one that inventory cites.

caveats: Offset Monte Carlo (input-offset-mc) was run at a FIXED 1.20 V supply only: five <corner>_mismatch sections x {-40, 27, 125} degC. The supply axis (1.08 V / 1.32 V) is covered only by the deterministic systematic-offset record; no statistical figure here is a statement about 1.08 V or 1.32 V.

Systematic and statistical offset are distinct evidence: the ratified bound is the systematic (nominal-device) half [DR-2]; the mismatch-driven 3σ half is measured [P] and is not ratified (DR-0002 residual (b), pending its own two-key pass). This report does not combine them into a ratified total.

The CMRR row is ratified on its mismatch-inclusive figure [DR-4], whose definition (Av0 minus the +3σ point of the drawn-Acm distribution, mean + 3σ in the LINEAR domain, N = 300 + process corners) is part of the number. This report reads that per-point figure from the record and re-derives it from the record's own linear mean and σ (definition check cmrr_linear_3sigma); it never aggregates in the dB domain. The superseded systematic floor is shown as context only.
Output swing is unloaded (CL = 2 pF, no resistive load): an upper bound. PSRR+ is ratified at the DC shelf and is strongly frequency-dependent.
Every measured row comes from nominal-device deterministic benches except the two Monte Carlo records (offset, CMRR); no other row carries a statistical basis.

Bound precision is an open spec question, not settled by this report: four DR-0002 bounds (DC gain >= 37.8 dB, integrated noise <= 108.9 µVrms, systematic offset <= 21.9 mV, swing span >= 0.571 V) are stricter than the raw worst case of the very records DR-0002 cites, which only round onto them (37.7812 dB, 108.949 µVrms, 21.927 mV, 0.570958 V). This report compares literally, so those rows FAIL. Whether to restate the bounds or ratify a comparison convention is for the keys in a decision record: 2AMLogic/sg13g2-opamp#101.
